headline: Spain Beat Argentina 1-0 in Extra Time to Win the World Cup
whyCareReason: The biggest night of the expanded World Cup: Spain outlast Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium.
teaser: Spain are world champions. A 1-0 extra-time win over Argentina at MetLife ends the first 48-team World Cup.
story:
MetLife Stadium held a final that had been building for a month. Spain brought the midfield distances that carried them through every knockout round. Argentina brought champion steel and a chase for back-to-back titles.

Regulation finished 0-0. Spain outshot Argentina by a huge margin. Argentina, down to ten after Enzo Fernandez was sent off, did not register a shot in normal time. Extra time finally broke. Nico Williams headed a ball into space. Ferran Torres, on as a substitute, scored in the 106th minute.

Spain 1-0 after extra time. Second World Cup, first since 2010. Attendance 80,663. Referee Slavko Vincic. Torres was man of the match. Emiliano Martinez made 11 saves, a World Cup final record.
stakes: The FIFA World Cup. Spain lift the trophy. Argentina finish runners-up.
rivalryAngle: Style clash at the absolute peak: Spanish positional control against Argentina's structure, moments of magic and final experience.
funFacts: Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute from a Nico Williams header.
Spain conceded one goal in eight matches, a record for a World Cup champion.
Spain became the first nation to hold the men's and women's World Cups at the same time.

keyPlayers.name: Ferran Torres
keyPlayers.hook: Came on in the 62nd minute and scored the only goal, in the 106th, from a Nico Williams header.

keyPlayers.name: Emiliano Martinez
keyPlayers.hook: Eleven saves in a World Cup final, a record, and still on the losing side.

headToHead: Major-tournament meetings between Spain and Argentina remain rare at this stage, which only raised the intrigue of the MetLife final.
